description: Save the game's dashboard: its pages, in the order the sidebar shows them. Each page is a board of panels in the game's own words, or a built-in view (events, performance, errors, players, heatmaps, sessions, versions, live, reports, servers, matches) the game keeps, renames or drops. Design it for this game, not for a genre it isn't: a puzzle game cares about solve time and hints, a mobile game about opens, modes, the paywall and purchases (revenue: a stat with sum "amount" of "purchase"; revenue per player: per "$players"; conversion: event "purchase" per "$players"; revenue by item: a breakdown with sum, of completed ones only with event "purchase:result=done"; a Roblox game's money is in Robux: currency "ROBUX", and devex true on a panel adds an estimate in dollars), a platformer about deaths per level (and a positions panel for where on a level they die). For a game on several platforms, a breakdown by $platform splits players or an event between them (iOS vs Android, PC vs Mac vs Steam Deck); a web game splits by $browser, and any game by $device_tier. For balance and outcomes, a breakdown with rate gives each row its rate and interval next to the overall one (win rate by hero: event "match_end", by "hero", rate "won"); per "$hours" turns counts and sums into rates per hour played (gold per hour); a distribution panel or a stat with of and quantile shows how long matches or runs last; a stat with first gives the median seconds from a session's start to its first event of a kind (time in the lobby: first "hall_left"), and one with never the share of ended sessions that never sent it (never left the lobby), so the game needn't time it by hand; a breakdown of steps or days takes order "value" (day 1 to 7 in order); a table lists an event's events one by one, grouped and sorted (daily runs by day, best score first: type "table", event "daily_run", group_by "day_label", sort "-score", of "score"); a list attribute (deck, build, boons) splits by element. Split by what the game set for the session with setProperties ($rank, $class, $region), and give a page where to show only some sessions (a page for the high ranks); a levels panel by a levelStart attribute shows clears by tier or difficulty, and count "runs" runs per biome. A multiplayer game gets a Network page (ping_p95 and disconnect_pct stats, net panels by $region or $link), and one whose dedicated servers run the SDK in server mode a Servers page (servers_now, server_tick_p95, a servers panel by players) or the built-in servers view; a game that sets match groups can keep the built-in matches view. An open world or an avatar hub that names its zones (setZone) gets where play time goes and how each zone runs: a breakdown by $zone without event (time in each zone), zone_time_pct and zone_median_s stats with zone, and frame_time by $zone (hitches per zone); don't send zone timing as custom events. The first page opens first. Use the events the game sends (glitchless_events lists them, with their attributes); on a board, stats first, then the game's own events and funnels, then levels, frame_time and errors. Leave out what the game has no data for (no Heatmaps page for a game without positions, no reports page for a game that doesn't turn bug reports on). Send every page: read the current ones with glitchless_dashboard (its spec), change them, send them all back. Pass reset: true to go back to the automatic dashboard. accent sets the colour of the game's boards and share links (links, the selected page, stats, the main chart series, the map), logo and banner their logo and header picture (the game's key art, behind each board's title), and background gives a level, a zone or the whole game a heatmap background (a top-down picture and its world bounds); each can be sent alone. A picture is a file on this computer, which the local server (npx glitchless-mcp) reads, or base64. The hosted server can't read your files: for file (or upload: true on any server) it answers with an upload link instead, and you send the picture with one curl (curl -X PUT --data-binary @file '<link>', no key). A link lasts 10 minutes, takes one picture for its one slot (the logo, the banner, or one place's background with the bounds it was made with) and then stops working; a picture refused for its size or type can be sent again until it expires, and a game gets at most 30 links an hour. Each slot's limit: a logo at most 100 KB and 1024 × 1024 pixels, a banner 300 KB and 4096 × 2048, a background 256 KB and 4096 × 4096, all PNG, JPEG or WebP. Needs a secret key with the dashboard scope.

accent.description: The accent colour of the game's boards and share links, "#rrggbb" (the game's own colour, such as its logo's), or null for none. Kept apart from the pages: send it alone to change only the colour. The dashboard darkens or lightens it where it would be hard to read. The logo and the banner (key art) are logo and banner here

background.description: A place's heatmap background, so the Heatmaps view and positions panels (where players went and died) read as the room they happened in: a top-down picture of a hub, a lobby or a level and the world bounds its edges stand for, with no SDK code. The place is a level, a zone the game sets with setZone, or neither: the whole game, for a game whose players move about with no level set (a hub); a zone with no picture of its own uses the whole game's. With axis xz (seen from above, the default) the picture's left edge is bounds.min[0] (x) and its right edge bounds.max[0], its top edge bounds.min[1] (z) and its bottom edge bounds.max[1]; with xy (a side view) its top is bounds.max[1] (y). Get the bounds from the game's own level data (the floor's corners), not by guessing. An upload is drawn over whatever an SDK captured for that place; remove: true goes back to the capture. PNG, JPEG or WebP, at most 256 KB and 4096 pixels a side: a JPEG about 1024 pixels across fits. Send it alone to change only the background, one place a call; glitchless_dashboard lists the game's backgrounds

axis.description: xz: seen from above, x across and z down the picture (default); xy: a side view, x across and y up

bounds.description: The world coordinates the picture covers on the axis's two coordinates: { "min": [x, z], "max": [x, z] } for xz, e.g. { "min": [-120, -80], "max": [120, 80] }

file.description: The picture: a PNG, JPEG or WebP file on this computer. The local server (npx glitchless-mcp) reads it; the hosted one answers with an upload link to send it to with one curl

image.description: Or the picture as base64 (or a data: URL); a big one is long in a call, so prefer file

level.description: The level, as the game passes it to levelStart

remove.description: Remove this place's uploaded background (an SDK's capture, if any, shows again)

upload.description: Answer with an upload link instead of saving now: send the picture to it with one curl (curl -X PUT --data-binary @file '<link>') within 10 minutes; it takes one picture and needs no key. The hosted server does this for file by itself

zone.description: Or the zone, as the game passes it to setZone (leave out level and zone for the whole game)

banner.description: The game's banner (its key art), the header behind each board's title, with a dark scrim so the title reads on any picture: PNG, JPEG or WebP, at most 300 KB and 4096 × 2048 pixels; the dashboard crops it to 1600 × 400 around its focus (a short strip on a phone), so a wide picture works best. Use the game's own key art or a capture of it from its files; ask before making one up

file.description: A PNG, JPEG or WebP file on this computer. The local server (npx glitchless-mcp) reads it; the hosted one answers with an upload link to send it to with one curl

focus.description: What stays in view when the banner is cropped to a strip (default center); can be sent alone

image.description: Or the picture as base64 (or a data: URL); a banner is long in a call, so prefer file

upload.description: Answer with an upload link instead of saving now: send the picture to it with one curl (curl -X PUT --data-binary @file '<link>') within 10 minutes; it takes one picture and needs no key. The hosted server does this for file by itself

currency.description: The game's one currency for money panels, an ISO 4217 code such as "USD", or "ROBUX" for a Roblox game's Robux (shown with ⬡; a panel's devex adds an estimate in dollars) (default: the one most of its purchases are sent in). Send it again with every save: glitchless_dashboard's spec has it

game.description: The game, by name or id, when signed in to a workspace (glitchless_list_games lists them); later calls keep it. With a key for one game (gl_sk_…), a call that names another game is refused: sign in to the workspace to reach every game.

logo.description: The game's logo, shown by its name on its boards and share links: PNG, JPEG or WebP (never SVG), at most 100 KB and 1024 × 1024 pixels; the dashboard fits it inside 256 px. Use the game's own logo or icon from its files; ask before making one up

file.description: A PNG, JPEG or WebP file on this computer. The local server (npx glitchless-mcp) reads it; the hosted one answers with an upload link to send it to with one curl

image.description: Or the picture as base64 (or a data: URL); a banner is long in a call, so prefer file

upload.description: Answer with an upload link instead of saving now: send the picture to it with one curl (curl -X PUT --data-binary @file '<link>') within 10 minutes; it takes one picture and needs no key. The hosted server does this for file by itself

pages.description: Every page, in order: at most 20 (boards and built-in views together)

items.description: One page: either panels (a board) or view (a built-in view)

id.description: Short id used in the page address, e.g. "money" (default: from the title)

options.description: live view: events, only these event names or types

panels.description: A board: its panels, in order

avg.description: stat, series, breakdown: a numeric attribute's mean per event instead of a count, e.g. "duration_s" by mode

bin.description: positions: a bin's width in world units for deaths (default about a hundredth of the place). A path's bins are about 64 across the place and never finer than bin, so on a 150-unit hub a path's bin is at least 5. Fix it when a game draws the panel, so bins don't move as the place fills in

bins.description: distribution: how many histogram bars, 2 to 40 (default 20). Bars are equal round steps from the 1st to the 99th percentile; under and over count what falls outside

by.description: series, breakdown, distribution: the attribute to split by, e.g. "mode" or "what" (a list attribute splits by element: each card of a deck gets a row, and an event counts once under each), or $version / $level / $zone (where the player was in an open world, setZone), or a split of the sessions that sent the event: $platform (Windows, macOS, Linux, Steam Deck, iOS, Android, Web…), $browser (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge…; a native build is "Godot app", "Unity app" and so on, a web build "Unity web build"), $device_tier (High-end, Mid-range, Low-end GPU, Software rendering: the tiers the Performance view uses, high to low), $link (Wi-Fi, Mobile data, Wired), or a session property the game sets with setProperties ($rank, $class, $region: sessions without it are "(none)", 40 values at most); counts only, no sum, over 31 days or less. levels and deaths: an attribute of the level's start ("tier", "party_size", a list such as "build"), a property or a split. net: $version, $level, $zone, a split or a property. servers: "players" (connected, in tenths of capacity), $level or $version. retention: a property ($spender). frame_time: $zone or $level, a row per value with frame time p50, p95, p99, frames over budget, hitches per minute played and its share of play time. versions: also a property ($class), its values side by side. A breakdown (by count) can also split by a Steam fact of the sessions that sent the event: $steam_branch, $steam_build, $steam_hardware, $steam_controller, $steam_language, $proton, $big_picture, $family_shared, $timed_trial. versions: $steam_branch or $steam_build compares Steam branches or builds on this page's stats instead of versions (the beta against "public"); needs a game that uses Steamworks

columns.description: table: the columns in order, up to 12: attributes of the event ("score", "attempt"), or $time, $version, $platform, $level, $session (a link to the session; numbered on a share link, never its ID). { "key": "duration_s", "unit": "s" } gives one a unit. Default: the event's own attributes, up to 8, without group_by

count.description: levels: "runs" counts each run (setGroup("run")) once at each level it reached, however many sessions it spanned: a roguelite's runs that reach each biome

devex.description: stat, series, breakdown with sum, in Robux: also give what the Robux would be worth in US dollars at Roblox's DevEx rate (devex: {estimate: true, robux, usd, rate, since, source}; a breakdown's rows each get usd). Always an estimate: it is the price players paid at DevEx's standard rate, and what the experience can cash out is less. Other currencies get devex null

event.description: stat, series, breakdown, distribution, table: one event, "name", "name=value" or "name:key=value". A list attribute (a deck, a build) matches when it has the value, and "battle_end:deck=hog_rider+ice_spirit" when it has all of them (any pair or trio). A series or breakdown by $platform, $browser or $device_tier can leave it out: then it counts sessions (and players, with player IDs) in each. A breakdown by $zone without it is the time played in each zone (frame time drawn there, paused in the background): each row's seconds, share_pct of all play, the sessions that went there (sessions_pct of all), players and median_s, their median time in it; time outside every zone is "(none)"

events.description: live: only these event names or types, e.g. ["buy", "paywall", "error"]

expect.description: breakdown or stat with rate: the percentage the game intends, such as a gacha's published odds (0.6 for 0.6%). Rows whose interval misses it are marked, and a finding names them

first.description: stat, instead of event: the seconds from a session's start to its first event like this one, the median over the sessions that sent it (or quantile): how long players stay in the lobby before they first leave it (first "hall_left"), the time to the first purchase ("purchase:result=done"). Works for events a Roblox server sends for a player (they go in that player's session, so it counts from joining). Replaces sending the seconds by hand. Over 31 days or less

group_by.description: table: rows go under one header per value of this attribute (or $version, $level, $platform), newest group first; events without it go under "(none)", last

label.description: levels: what the game calls a level, e.g. "Stop" or "Puzzle"

level.description: positions: the level id, as the game passes it to levelStart (or zone, or neither for the whole game: a hub with no levels). levels and deaths: only this level's rows

limit.description: How many: errors, findings, reports and breakdown rows up to 20, sessions up to 50, series lines up to 8, distribution rows up to 8, retention days up to 90 (default 14), table rows per group up to 100 (default 20; at most 30 groups, the rest counted in more_groups)

measure.description: store_revenue (required): revenue (in the window), per_player (over the players Glitchless measured), by_day (revenue), by_version, by_country (a world map of installs and revenue, and a list: country, installs, revenue, purchases; RevenueCat's countries come with each hourly sync, Stripe's have revenue only); RevenueCat only: installs (new customers, next to Glitchless's new players), active_users (a day), mrr, actives (active subscriptions), trials (active trials), players_by_day (installs and active users), by_store (revenue by store next to the sessions on its platform); Stripe only: refunds (and disputes), customers (new paying customers), by_product; Roblox: revenue, per_player, by_day (in Robux), installs (new users), active_users (daily active users), players_by_day, and retention (D1, D7, D30 by cohort day, size m)

metric.description: stat: sessions, players, avg_session_s, median_session_s, crash_free_pct, error_free_pct, frame_p95, avg_fps, hitches_per_min, errors, deaths, rage_quit_pct, hours_played (the time the game was on screen), players_now (sessions playing in the last two minutes, whatever the range), runs (each run once). Network (multiplayer): ping_p50, ping_p95 (ms), loss_pct, disconnects_per_hour, disconnect_pct (level attempts a disconnect ended). Servers (from the game's servers in server mode): servers_now (running now, with the players connected to them), server_tick_p95, server_crash_free_pct, players_per_server. Zones (a game that sets them with setZone; give zone): zone_time_pct (the zone's share of play time), zone_median_s (the median time in it of the sessions that went there). deaths and errors take per "$hours": deaths per hour played

min.description: breakdown with rate or avg: rows with fewer events are left out and counted in small (default 30 for a rate, 10 for an average)

never.description: stat, instead of event: the share of the window's ended sessions that never sent this event (ended: sent session_end, or nothing for 30 minutes), with count and base: players who never left the lobby (never "hall_left"), never bought. Sessions still playing aren't counted. Over 31 days or less

note.description: One line on why this panel matters: people read it behind the info icon next to the panel's title

of.description: distribution (required), stat: the numeric attribute whose spread to show, e.g. "duration_s". A stat with of and quantile shows one percentile: the median match. table: the numeric attribute whose lowest, average and highest each group header shows, e.g. "score"

order.description: breakdown: the rows' order, before the top limit rows are taken. count (the most events first) or value (in the values' own natural order: streak days 1, 2 … 10, heat 0, 1, 2) on any breakdown; with rate or avg also rate or avg (their default, the highest first). Without one, a count breakdown is the most first and a sum the largest first

per.description: stat: divide by this event to get a percentage (event "buy=done" per "paywall"); or "$players" / "$sessions": the share of them that sent the event (conversion), or with sum, the sum per player or session (revenue per player); or "$hours": per hour played (matches per hour, with sum XP or gold per hour). series, breakdown: "$hours", each bucket or row per hour played (by $version or $level each over its own hours, by an attribute every row over the window's)

quantile.description: stat with of or first: the percentile, 1 to 99 (50: the median, 90: 1 in 10 is over it; first defaults to 50)

rate.description: stat, series, breakdown: the share of the event's events where a flag holds, "won" (a boolean, or a number that is only 1 or 0), or a word outcome holds, "result=win". A breakdown gives each row its rate with a 95% interval (low, high) next to the overall rate: win rate by hero, by heat, of decks with each card (by a list), boons taken when offered. Send outcomes as booleans where you can: a word outcome split by another attribute reads the first 16 of each session's events

sent.description: sessions: only sessions that sent this event, e.g. "buy=done"

show.description: positions: deaths (default), path (where players went, on a coarser grid) or both. store_revenue by_country: installs (default) or revenue, what its map shows first (people can switch). net: ping (default), loss or disconnects. servers: ticks (default), players or crashes

size.description: s = a quarter row (stats), m = half, l = full width

sort.description: table: the rows' order inside each group, an attribute or $time, $version, $platform, $level, "-" first for highest first: "-score" (default "-$time", the newest first). Events without the value go last

steps.description: funnel: events in order, comma-separated, e.g. "paywall,buy=tapped,buy=done"

store.description: store_reviews, store_players, store_sales, store_vitals, store_score: the store (default: the game's first connected one; Roblox has no reviews); store_revenue: revenuecat, stripe or roblox

sum.description: stat, series, breakdown: add up this numeric attribute instead of counting events, e.g. "amount" of "purchase" for revenue. Money (events with a currency, an ISO code or "ROBUX") shows in the game's currency; amounts in another currency are named, never added (Robux are never added to dollars). The event can be filtered, also split by an attribute: revenue of completed purchases by item is event "purchase:result=done", by "item", sum "amount" (read from each session's first 16 of the event), so cancelled purchases can carry their amount too

title.description: In the game's own words, e.g. "Stops won vs lost"

type.description: distribution: how a numeric attribute (of) spreads, as percentiles (p50, p90, p99) and a histogram, optionally by a split: match length, time in queue, placement, floors reached. levels: starts, completions, fails, deaths and disconnects per level, with the median and p90 clear time; by splits each level's attempts (clears by tier, by class), count "runs" counts runs per biome. retention: D1, D7 and D30 by the day players were first seen; needs player IDs (privacy install or full); by a property, per value. positions: where players died on one level, in one zone, or anywhere in the game (a hub or lobby with no level set), and where they went, as counts per bin over the place's background (glitchless_set_dashboard's background uploads one): safe on a shared board, and a game can poll it through a share link to draw its own dead. net (a multiplayer game): show ping (p50 and p95 over time, and the share of play over 150 ms), loss, or disconnects (per hour played, by reason), optionally by a split ($region, $link, $level, $version). servers (a game whose dedicated servers run the SDK in server mode): show ticks (tick time against its budget, by "players" connected, $level or $version), players, or crashes (with the matches and players each ended). table: one event's events listed one by one (each a row of its attributes, time, version, platform, level or session), grouped by an attribute with each group's events, sessions and the lowest, average and highest of a number: daily runs by day with their scores, runs by seed, matches by mode. Only track() events have rows (count() sends totals); a session keeps its first 16 of each event For a game connected to a store (Steam; give store): store_reviews (reviews over time and by build, with what was measured on each), store_vitals (the store's own vitals by version (Google Play: slow rendering, crashes, ANRs; the App Store: hangs, launch, hitches; Roblox: crash rate, crashes and frame rate by place version, and by platform) next to what Glitchless measured, with where they disagree), store_players (players online (Steam) or playing now (Roblox) next to the sessions measured: telemetry coverage), store_sales (units, returns and wishlists by day; on Steam needs the Financial API key), store_score (a store's rating, small (size s): the average stars of the written reviews synced in the window and how many, next to the store's own overall rating where it has one (the App Store: Apple's rating and rating count; Steam: its review summary). Google Play has no API for its overall rating, so it shows the synced reviews' average and says so. Roblox: its thumbs up and down, favorites and visits. One panel per store), store_revenue (real revenue from RevenueCat (store revenuecat) or the game's own Stripe account (store stripe); give measure: revenue in the window, revenue per player measured, revenue per day next to the game's own purchase events, revenue by version next to what Glitchless measured, or a world map of revenue by country with a ranked list (by_country, size l); RevenueCat also installs (its new customers) next to Glitchless's new players, active users a day, MRR, active subscriptions, active trials, installs and active users per day, installs on the map, and revenue by store (App Store, Google Play) next to the iOS and Android sessions Glitchless measured (by_store); Stripe also refunds (and disputes), new paying customers and revenue by product (by version from the purchases the game tied to a session); Roblox (store roblox): Robux earned and per player, its daily active users (active_users) and new users (installs), both per day, and retention (D1, D7, D30 by cohort day: the only retention a Roblox game has, since its SDK is anonymous))

unit.description: distribution, stat with of: what the numbers are in, shown after them ("s" reads as minutes or hours when large, or the game's own word: "floors")

zone.description: positions: the zone instead of a level, as the game passes it to setZone, e.g. "hall". Leave out level and zone for every position and death in the game

title.description: The name in the sidebar, in the words the game uses (a view keeps its built-in name without one)

view.description: A built-in view instead of panels (reports: the bug reports players sent, with their screenshots; servers: the game's dedicated servers in server mode, their ticks by map and players connected, crashes and memory; matches: the range's matches, each opening a match page with every player's ping slot by slot and the server's ticks under them)

where.description: A board page only: the session properties its sessions must have, "$<key>" → a value or a list of up to 20 (at most 4 properties), e.g. { "$rank": ["diamond", "master"] }: every panel on the page reads only those sessions (a "Diamond and up" page)

reset.description: Delete the saved dashboard and go back to the automatic one

service.description: Game service name (defaults to the most recently active game)

name: glitchless_set_dashboard
title: Save dashboard
